B-B3.statement: Runtime-verified: GET /api/workspaces/ws_apollo/items?sort= and ?sort (valueless) return 200 with default updated_desc order. The contract defines 'absent' (default) and three exact valid values; any other explicit value is 'explicit invalid' -> 400 validation_failed with fields.sort. An explicitly present empty value is most literally an explicit invalid value. Candidate-a returns 400 for both inputs.
B-B3.evidence: probe.mjs candidate-b output line '?sort= (empty) 200' and '?sort= (no value) 200' (CHECKS.md C10)
B-B3.fix: Treat an explicitly present sort value (including empty string) that is not one of the three as 400 validation_failed with the exact fields.sort string; alternatively obtain a frozen evaluator ruling that empty == absent before dispatch.

ordering_strategy_comparison: Both candidates embed the identical three ORDER BY clauses (updatedAt DESC + id BINARY ASC; updatedAt ASC + id BINARY DESC; title NOCASE ASC + id BINARY ASC). candidate-a interpolates a validated suffix into one prepared statement; candidate-b selects among three full statements. Both validate only after auth (401) and membership/resource (404), per FAQ #5 query precedence. Both are injection-safe (fixed maps; no user input reaches SQL text). Runtime-verified identical item orders for all valid values; the strategies differ only in validation style, which produced the B-B3 empty-value divergence.
